sources.note: Parallel lookups over multiple disjoint paths and crypto-puzzle friction remain the secure-routing teacher.
Record validation/selection and provider liveness/reachability keep shaping provider proof and mutable-head validators.
Ed25519/salt/sequence/signature/CAS remains the compact mutable-slot teacher; rev0013 adds local history and path pressure around it.
The spirit of constraining cheap targeted node ID choice remains useful, though I2P destinations require different binding than IPs.
Specialized indexers/garden nodes may need sampled views, but sampling can become a metadata and abuse surface.
Sloppy storage and cluster/latency awareness remain useful for garden cache and hot-key work.
Stable mutable identifiers, capabilities, and untrusted servers able to deny/rollback but not read/modify remain strong mutability teachers.
SAM remains likely for Python/non-Java experiments; docs stress long-lived sessions and note Java I2P/i2pd feature differences.

rev0013_design_delta: Provider proof handshakes, mutable-head witness pressure, latency forge, and cube audit/refactor are now toy-tested surfaces.
